## Design

### 2026-10-08 – ![AtlasTag Global Tracking Poster](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/w890EgVDHUHryLXezmpxYEln7rcgrK0C/82f13571bddfde49df86fc792f5c40ac02910586da929b369e8ccf5a2bf2f738.pn

**1.13h**

![AtlasTag Global Tracking Poster](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/w890EgVDHUHryLXezmpxYEln7rcgrK0C/82f13571bddfde49df86fc792f5c40ac02910586da929b369e8ccf5a2bf2f738.png)

- Started building the foundation for AtlasTag.
- Set up the GitHub repository and development workflow.
- Documented the initial requirements and system architecture.
- Researched cellular + GNSS modules, motion sensors, power management, storage, SIMs, and antennas.
- Started building the BOM with real Indian component pricing.
- Compared different approaches for making AtlasTag compact, battery-powered, and globally connected.
- Identified the cellular + GNSS platform as the biggest decision before moving into PCB design.
What I learned:
- Hardware design starts with making the right architectural decisions.
- Choosing the wrong cellular/GNSS platform can affect the PCB, power, firmware, antenna, size, and cost.
- I need to validate the core hardware before jumping into PCB design.
Next:
- Deep-dive into the cellular + GNSS options.
- Finalize the core hardware platform.
- Start moving from research → actual PCB design.
